_about: The dashboard To-Do feed: a short, layman-readable daily checklist of curation work (for Sam) and engineering/pre-curation work (for Fable, the Claude session), rendered by cpl_todos.js as the 📋 button on every tab. Refreshed at every Rule 8 checkpoint alongside the session handoff.
_as_of: 2026-08-13 · SkyPeak — POST's ten credit recommendations are published, and Sierra still can't read them.
_status: Two wrong Sierra answers turned out to be the same problem, and it wasn't the one it looked like. Asked what Cerritos might adopt for POST, Sierra named one course; there are ten. Asked about Cerritos and ironworkers she said there was none; there is plenty. In both cases the right answer was already in our data — it had just never been copied to the one place Sierra can read. POST's full set of ten (eight C-ID courses plus two electives) has been sitting in the same file that feeds the public CPL Fact Sheet all along. That set is now published for all 2,205 credentials, and where a credential has no statewide standard we publish the most common recommendations across the colleges that use it, with the number of colleges behind each. Separately, Sierra had been calling 42 statewide credentials 'local' — including Paramedic License — because the flag was read from the wrong one of two files. That is corrected. IMPORTANT: none of this changes what Sierra says yet. The data is in place; connecting her to it is one more piece of work, and it is the next thing. Also shipped: you can now edit a Sierra instruction after saving it, and test it without leaving the tab.

items.text: THE NEXT THING. Connect Sierra to the new credit-recommendation table and deploy her. Until that happens she still answers POST with one course, even though all ten are published. Same piece of work should fix the Cerritos ironworker answer and stop ready-to-adopt exhibits from being sorted last.

Cerritos ironworker CPL reads as zero because the exhibit list stores the titles as 'FIW Orientation' and 'IW- Mixed Base' — no 'iron' anywhere — while the curated list has 16 Cerritos credentials, 11 of them named 'Ironworker Apprenticeship'. Sierra searches the raw titles and never checks the curated names. Also: searching the plural 'ironworkers' returns nothing at all.

Sam's rule: exhibits created before any college adopts them are deliberate, and should be prominent choices for adoption. Right now the adoption suggestions are ordered by how many colleges already use something, which puts a brand-new ready-to-adopt exhibit dead last — exactly backwards.

25 pieces of feedback on Sierra have never been looked at, the oldest since 1 July. The tab is now easy to use — you can mark what you've read, and write an instruction straight from a bad answer. Worth half an hour.

Three instructions you wrote on 12 August were cut off at 500 characters before that limit was fixed, and the lost text can't be recovered. You can now edit an instruction after saving it, so retyping them is quicker than it was.

12 credentials are marked statewide in the adoption file but don't exist in the credential list at all, so the statewide fix couldn't reach them. Worth finding out whether they're renames or genuinely missing.

The test file for the funding tab runs for over four minutes and never finishes, so the full test suite can't complete. It is not a new problem — that file hasn't changed — but it means nobody is running the whole suite.

Now that Contracts is locked to the Finance phrase, tell whoever works the contract register what the new phrase is. Until they have it they will see a locked page — with a box to type it into, but nothing to type. Nobody else is affected; every other tab still takes the general team phrase.

A decision only you can make, and it is live now rather than hypothetical: someone holding the Finance phrase can also open every shared CPL tab — budget, personnel, projects, MAP contacts. That is fine if everyone you give it to is trusted with all of it. If not, say so and the scopes get split.
Still waiting on the MAP deep links from Malone and Pedro. Three sections on My College are built and ready for them.
The college/district name crosswalk is built and merged but never written to Supabase — that write is what actually ends the 'Mt San Antonio vs Mt. San Antonio' mismatch.
